ambiguities.issue: The raw moment is not real-defined for every printed case p > 0 and every allowed real-valued X.
ambiguities.evidence: The source simultaneously permits real-valued X (PDF page 1, printed page 5, footnote 1) and states the raw moment as E X^p for p > 0 without an integer or nonnegativity restriction (selected sentence). In particular, p = 1/2 satisfies p > 0, while X^(1/2) is not real-valued where X < 0 under ordinary real arithmetic.
ambiguities.impact: The unrestricted real-p raw-moment clause is underspecified or ill-defined for negative-valued X. A formalization must not silently choose signed real power, complex power, absolute power, or an integer-only restriction, because none of those conventions is stated on this page.

contract_plain_english: On PDF page 1 (printed page 5), the book takes a real-valued random variable X on a probability space and says that, for p > 0, its p-th moment is the Lebesgue expectation of X^p and its p-th absolute moment is the expectation of |X|^p; omitted expectation brackets do not change that parsing. The absolute-moment expression is meaningful for arbitrary positive real p subject to the unstated expectation-existence convention. The raw-moment expression has a source-level obstruction: the page neither restricts p to integers nor restricts X to nonnegative values, so the literal range includes p = 1/2 even though X^(1/2) is not real-valued where X is negative. No convention resolving that obstruction appears in the selected page, and none may be guessed.
